subject: MAP: token budget reconciliation & eval milestones for HearthTech pilot
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@hearthtech.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Wells <sam.wells@hearthtech.com>, HearthTech Procurement <procure@hearthtech.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff and token-econ sanity check

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency and the structured output examples. We want to move to a short mutual action plan (MAP) and an evaluation window, but before we formalize dates procurement has asked for a concise reconciliation of the unit economics and the assumptions your team is using for tokens/$, caching, and batching. Specifically:

- Per-token pricing assumptions for staged models (hosted vs dedicated).
- Expected tokens per request for our chat flows (we estimate ~320 tokens avg).
- Caching assumptions (prefix/KV cache hit rate expectations).
- Typical batching behavior and latency impact (we have a 250 ms p99 SLO target).

Can you put together a short MAP doc with milestones, acceptance criteria for the eval, and a reconciled token budget so procurement has something they can sign off on? If helpful, I attached our internal forecast (small sample) — will share more on Monday.

Looking to get the MAP agreed by Oct 15 to keep the pilot on the timeline.

Best,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of AI Product, HearthTech

Attachment: hearthtech_forecast_sample.csv (csv, 12KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@hearthtech.com>
Cc: Sam Wells <sam.wells@hearthtech.com>, HearthTech Procurement <procure@hearthtech.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff and token-econ sanity check

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together a compact MAP and an assumptions sheet so procurement can see the reconciliation end-to-end. High level summary below; full MAP and assumptions attached (hearthtech_map_v1.xlsx, token_model_assumptions.pdf, redwood_eval_checklist.md).

Quick reconciled assumptions (conservative):
- Hosted model tier price: $0.0008 per token equivalent (in our catalog this maps to redwood-std-v1).
- Dedicated (reserved) effective price: $0.00045 per token equivalent (based on committed throughput and batching).
- HearthTech expected avg tokens per convo: 320 tokens/request (you estimated ~320; we used 340 to be conservative).
- Prefetch/prefix KV cache hit-rate assumption: 30% hit for stable prompts; 50% for identical prompt reuse (we use 30% as MAP baseline).
- Batching: average batch size 2.5 requests under target traffic pattern; peak batching may reach 4.5 which improves tokens/$ but increases queueing latency.
- Latency SLO: we can meet a 250 ms p99 with hosted for single-request flows at low concurrency; with batching enabled p99 may increase ~40–80 ms depending on batch size and queueing threshold.

MAP milestones & provisional timeline (requested sign-off by Oct 15):
- Oct 12: Agree token-econ baseline and acceptance criteria (this thread).
- Oct 20–23: Eval period kickoff (1 week smoke + 2 weeks full eval).
- Nov 6: Eval close, metrics review (tokens consumed, cache hit-rate, avg latency, tail latency).
- Nov 12: Procurement & contract signature target.

Acceptance criteria (for go/no-go):
- Tokens per successful convo within +/- 15% of reconciled baseline when measured at sample N=1,000 requests.
- Effective tokens/$ meets the committed budget within 20% (post-cache).
- Latency p99 <= 300 ms for interactive flows during normal concurrency.
- No functional regressions in structured output for the 10 eval prompts in the checklist.

Action items:
- Emma: confirm acceptance criteria or flag changes by EOD Oct 12.
- Procurement: confirm deal_id & desired billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly).
- HearthTech devs: provide 1,000 sample interactions (anonymized) by Oct 18.

I copied Camila and David for engineering confirmation of batching/caching assumptions.

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: hearthtech_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 68KB), token_model_assumptions.pdf (pdf, 42KB), redwood_eval_checklist.md (md, 6KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2026 12:07:00 -07:00

Camila / David — forwarding Emma's ask and the MAP I just sent. Two quick asks before I confirm to HearthTech: 

1) Camila: can you confirm the acceptance criteria phrasing for the eval (esp. the tokens/$ tolerance and the structured-output test)? We want something procurement-friendly.
2) David: please validate the caching & batching bullet points and whether our latency p99 delta estimates are realistic at the target batch sizes. If there's a mode or knob (e.g., max-wait-ms) we should call out, note it.

I plan to push this back to Emma once you both sign off.

—Markus

Thanks Mark — quick notes from SE side: 

- Acceptance criteria language tweak: change "Effective tokens/$ meets the committed budget within 20%" to "Effective tokens/$ at sample traffic must be <= committed budget + 20% (post-cache)" — makes it clearer to procurement.
- Add an explicit test case: 10 canonical prompts for structured output (we'll run auto-compare + human spot-check for the first 50 responses). Put those prompts in redwood_eval_checklist.md.
- For the token baseline, use 340 avg tokens/request (conservative). We'll instrument the sample harness to record both input and output tokens so the reconciliation is transparent.

I'll coordinate the sample harness and include the script in the Drive folder.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP kickoff and token-econ sanity check — batching/caching validation

Markus / Camila — reviewed and attached a short assumptions supplement (token_model_assumptions.pdf). Key engineering confirmations: 

- Prefetch/KV cache: baseline 30% hit is reasonable for HearthTech's flow based on the sample prompts Emma shared. We should run a quick local simulation, but use 30% in the MAP to stay conservative.
- Batching behavior: avg batch size 2.5 under steady-state RPS=40; p95 latency increases around +60 ms at avg batch 2.5 when we enforce max-wait-ms=15 to keep tail low. If HearthTech allows max-wait-ms=30 we can reduce cost by ~12% at the expense of ~25 ms additional p99.
- Tokens equivalence: we normalize all model outputs to a token equivalency metric that maps to the hosted pricing line. See token_model_assumptions.pdf for transformation and quantization adjustments.

I'll add a short benchmark run to the Drive folder; recommend we run it against the 1,000-sample harness during the smoke week (Oct 20–23) to validate.

-David
David Kim
Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_model_assumptions.pdf (pdf, 42KB)

Emma — circling back with the finalized MAP and the conservative token-econ baseline your procurement asked for. Attached are the MAP workbook, a short engineering assumptions PDF, and the eval checklist. Summary: 

- Baseline used for MAP: 340 tokens/req avg, 30% KV cache hit, avg batch 2.5, hosted price $0.0008/token eq, dedicated effective $0.00045/token eq.
- Eval period: Oct 20–Nov 6 (smoke tests Oct 20–23; full eval Oct 24–Nov 6).
- Go decision gates: meet acceptance criteria in the checklist; procurement to confirm billing cadence and sign deal_id DEAL-HT-8342 by Nov 12.

Please reply with a one-line sign-off on the acceptance criteria and the timeline (e.g., "HearthTech accepts the MAP baseline and timeline") so procurement has a trail. If you need any adjustments to the budget tolerance or the batch/wait knobs we can mark those as negotiable in contract addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
